# Neonix MCP

> Neonix is an HTML-to-motion-video compiler: it turns HTML and CSS into a real, exportable motion video.

Neonix MCP is the official Model Context Protocol server for Neonix. AI agents such as Claude,
ChatGPT, and Grok connect to it over Remote MCP to create, edit, preview, and export
motion-video projects from HTML and CSS.

## FAQ

Q: What is Neonix MCP?
A: The official remote MCP server for Neonix, an HTML-to-motion-video compiler. It exposes
tools for creating and editing video projects, authoring HTML/CSS, applying JSON patches,
managing assets, and exporting MP4 files.

Q: How do I connect to it?
A: Add a remote MCP server pointing at https://www.neonix.video/api/mcp and sign in with OAuth
when prompted. In Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http neonix https://neonix.video/api/mcp`.

Q: Do I need an API key?
A: No. Authentication is OAuth 2.1 — you sign in with your Neonix account and grant access.

Q: What does the server let an agent do?
A: Create and manage projects, read and edit HTML/CSS source, apply small JSON patches to the
compiled document, manage assets, and export a real MP4.

Q: How does Neonix turn HTML into video?
A: You or an AI agent write HTML and CSS describing a scene. Neonix compiles it into a
structured JSON document, which can be previewed and edited, then exports it to a real,
downloadable MP4.
